title: 'Let someone else do PM's tasks': CJP's Dipke says 'Modi good as influencer'
content: Abhijeet Dipke returned to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar after a student protest at Jantar Mantar. He warned the central government about continued student anger and potential future actions. Dipke alleged students faced harassment and intimidation instead of government dialogue. He criticized the Prime Minister and questioned the effectiveness of new laws. The student leader vowed to launch a larger agitation if necessary.

title: 'Demanded multiple relationships': IPS trainee charged with rape of colleague
content: A trainee IPS officer now faces rape and attempt-to-murder charges.  These new charges were added after the initial complaint of sexual assault.  The officer was previously arrested and sent to judicial remand for fourteen days.  The woman IPS trainee had lodged her complaint eleven days prior to the arrest.  The case involves allegations of sexual misconduct and privacy violations at SVPNPA.

title: 'Embarrassing': Former hockey captain slams India's blue jersey being replaced by saffron
content: Former India hockey captain Viren Rasquinha criticised Hockey India’s decision to replace the team’s iconic blue jersey with saffron ahead of the 2026 Hockey World Cup, calling it "embarrassing" and questioning the change. Hockey India said the new colour symbolises "courage, sacrifice & victory" and represents new beginnings. India’s men and women will begin their World Cup campaigns in Group D.

title: E20 petrol may harm BS-III vehicle rubber parts, says Nitin Gadkari
content: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari informed Rajya Sabha about E20 fuel impacts. Studies found no major performance impact on overall vehicle operations. BS-VI vehicles continue meeting emission norms when tested with E20 fuel. Legacy vehicles did not exhibit significant performance variations or abnormal wear. However, some BS-III vehicles may require rubber part replacements.

title: Brookfield joins US utility for $100 billion data centre at former nuclear site
content: Brookfield and NextEra Energy plan a significant data centre and energy complex. This massive project will be built on a former uranium enrichment site in Kentucky. The development includes substantial natural gas generation and battery storage capacity.  The privately financed campus is expected to begin operations in phases from 2028.  This initiative aligns with a White House pledge to manage AI infrastructure costs.

title: Record alert: Indian boxers eclipse Birmingham tally with 10 guaranteed medals
content: Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Arundhati Choudhary (70kg), Sachin Siwach (60kg), Ankush Panghal (80kg), Narender Berwal (+90kg) and world champion Jaismine Lamboria (57kg) joined Lovlina Borgohain (75kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg) and Jadumani Singh (55kg) in the semifinals of their respective weight categories. India had finished with seven boxing medals in Birmingham - three gold, one silver and three bronze.

title: Salman Rushdie stabbing: Attacker convicted on Hezbollah support, terror charges
content: A US man already serving a lengthy sentence was convicted on new federal charges.  He was found guilty of providing material support to the militant group Hezbollah.  Prosecutors linked his actions to a 1989 fatwa and a later speech.  The author Salman Rushdie testified during the federal trial about the attack.  This conviction adds to his existing sentence for attempted murder.

title: Crude prices retreat as oil continues flowing through Hormuz alternatives
content: Oil prices declined on Thursday after a significant rally the previous day. Crude oil continued to move out of the Middle East despite escalating conflict. Shipping activity indicated that oil supplies were still finding routes out of the region. Military actions intensified with US-Saudi strikes targeting Iran-backed forces in Iraq. Saudi Arabia is reportedly assembling a coalition to protect Red Sea shipping from Houthi attacks.

title: How Europe's heatwave is proving Americans right about air conditioning
content: Europeans are now buying air conditioning units in unprecedented numbers. This trend signals a significant cultural shift toward cooling solutions. Manufacturers report double-digit growth in sales across several European countries. Rising temperatures and extreme heat events are becoming impossible to ignore. This shift is driven by comfort and the growing recognition of heat as a public health risk.

title: We are in India, be realistic, says HC, lifts curbs on hotel over 2 insects
content: The Bombay high court quashed a hotel's license suspension after finding minor hygiene issues.  A solitary finding of two insects did not justify the continued suspension of the license.  The court accepted the hotel's undertaking to maintain high sanitation standards.  The Food and Drug Administration's drive aims to improve food safety across Maharashtra.  The court appreciated the state and FDA actions in enforcing food safety laws.

title: Remora hitches 19-minute ride as sea turtle lays eggs in Costa Rica
content: On a picturesque Costa Rican beach, an unexpected sight caught the eyes of researchers when a mother sea turtle arrived with a lively suckerfish clinging to her shell for an astonishing nineteen minutes. The fish, which seemed to adapt momentarily to land, showcased its gill movements. After careful observation, it was returned to its aquatic home, darting away with unexpected vigor, leaving onlookers astonished by its resilience.

title: 'Don’t get ‘shocked’ by healthcare costs': US billionaire Mark Cuban tells CEOs
content: Mark Cuban advises US chief executives to re-evaluate employee healthcare spending strategies.  He highlights that companies often overspend due to complex insurance contract complexities.  Cuban suggests using artificial intelligence tools to uncover hidden costs within these agreements.  He notes that human resources departments are frequently understaffed and overwhelmed with these duties.  This approach aims to improve financial efficiency and employee well-being for businesses.

title: Former CSK coach tipped for England's Test head coach role
content: Stephen Fleming is reportedly the frontrunner for England's Test head coach position. He has emerged as the preferred candidate after a thorough interview process. Fleming will replace Brendon McCullum, who is now leading England's white-ball teams. Fleming recently concluded a successful eighteen-year tenure with Chennai Super Kings. Joe Root will temporarily lead the team before Fleming's official start.

title: 2 years after death, SC clears ex-PM Manmohan Singh in Coalgate case
content: The Supreme Court has cleared former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in a coal block scam case. This decision comes more than eleven years after a Delhi court summoned him as an accused. The court closed the case nearly two years after his demise in November 2024. The apex court quashed the trial court's order taking cognisance of the crime.

title: Lamine Yamal says his mother's sacrifices outweigh childhood struggles he endured
content: Lamine Yamal, the 19-year-old World Cup winner, has spoken openly about a childhood shaped by financial hardship and parental sacrifice. His mother, Sheila Ebana, emigrated from Equatorial Guinea to Spain as a teenager, had Yamal at 16, and raised him largely alone after separating from his father when Lamine was three. Yamal credits her with shielding him from the worst of their circumstances, saying she made him see only the beautiful side of life. He also reflected on his rapid rise at Barcelona, describing himself as a creative and entertaining player who never anticipated reaching the first team quite so quickly

title: Candace Owens shares unseen Charlie Kirk video as Alex Jones questions narrative
content: Candace Owens has released new rooftop footage that she says raises questions about whether Tyler Robinson was the person who shot Charlie Kirk. Alex Jones backed her claims, arguing the video contradicts the official case against Robinson. However, authorities still identify Robinson as the accused, and a judge has not yet ruled on whether the case will move to trial.

title: Gisele Bündchen opens up on motherhood struggles during marriage to Tom Brady
content: Tom Brady's ex wife Gisele Bündchen has gone more and more public about their lives ever since the two ended thir marriage. The Brazilian supermodel has now opened up about motherhood.

title: CWG: Sreeshankar wins long jump silver; Gavit claims Games record gold
content: Sreeshankar continued his impressive run at the Commonwealth Games by winning silver in the men's long jump with a best effort of 8.09m. He had also finished second at the 2022 Games, becoming the first Indian to win back-to-back Commonwealth Games medals in the event.

title: IIT-B alumnus Aphale named Ram temple trust’s first secretary, will oversee transactions
content: Jagdish Aphale, an IIT Bombay alumnus, has been appointed the Ayodhya Ram temple trust's first secretary. He will also serve as a joint signatory for financial transactions, enhancing accountability. This appointment follows recent resignations and alleged donation theft issues. Aphale previously supervised construction at the temple complex for nearly four years. His integration into the trust's internal processes has been ongoing for two weeks.

title: DGCA-ordered probe cleared Dreamliner fuel switch: Government
content: A Boeing probe found no abnormality in the B787 fuel control switch locking mechanism. This examination was ordered by the DGCA after a crew reported an issue post-landing. The switches control fuel supply and have faced scrutiny after a past crash incident. Further inspection of the complete thrust control module at the OEM facility is currently underway.

title: Denied seat, student hacks IIT-Kanpur website to show his 'merit'
content: A BTech applicant hacked IIT Kanpur's website seeking admission consideration. He claimed he was denied a fair chance in the selection process. The IIT director invited the candidate to campus for an assessment. He stressed that hacking was not the correct approach to gain entry. The institute will consider him if genuine talent is demonstrated.

title: Continue with your duties fearlessly, CRPF chief tells troopers amid pellet gun row
content: CRPF Director General G P Singh supports troops acting in good faith during duty.  He assures responsibility for all decisions made in the public interest.  An internal probe found standard operating procedures were followed by RAF personnel.  Pellet guns were used after other crowd dispersal methods failed.  This investigation may prevent charges against the RAF personnel involved.

title: 'Not going to let him get away': Rahul targets Shah over police action on NEET protesters
content: Rahul Gandhi accused Home Minister Amit Shah of police excesses against protesters.  He demanded Shah's dismissal and a Supreme Court-monitored probe into the actions.  Gandhi also blamed the RSS for the education sector's current problems.  Government ministers challenged Gandhi to provide proof or issue an apology.  The Lok Sabha experienced disruptions over these serious allegations.

title: Need to reinvent ways to deal with global challenges: Finance ministry
content: India's economy shows resilience despite global challenges and uncertainties.  Swift policy responses and implementation are crucial for attracting investment.  Rising crude oil prices pose a potential pressure on fiscal and current accounts.  The external sector remains resilient due to strong exports and remittances.  Adverse weather conditions present a risk to farm output and rural demand.

title: 'Jana Nayagan' BO day 7: Vijay's film sees a midweek dip, earns Rs 6.10cr
content: Jana Nayagan experienced a box office slowdown on its seventh day. The action drama earned over six crore rupees on Wednesday. Its India net collection has now surpassed one hundred forty-nine crore rupees. Overseas collections have pushed the worldwide gross to over two hundred fifty-five crore rupees. The Tamil version continues to be the film's biggest contributor.

title: Ahead of dengue vaccine rollout, all 4 strains found in circulation
content: India's first dengue virus mapping shows all four serotypes circulating in eight states.  This finding could influence the country's upcoming dengue vaccine strategy.  Researchers found DENV-2 to be the dominant circulating strain across the nation.  Concurrent infections with multiple strains are linked to more severe dengue disease.  Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for monitoring virus circulation and guiding policy.

title: Guard's accidental gunshot kills man visiting bank in city
content: A customer was killed Tuesday after a security guard's gun discharged accidentally. Manish Kumar, a farmer, was updating his Aadhaar card at the Union Bank branch. The ex-serviceman guard, Vinod Kumar, was loading cartridges when the firearm discharged. The bullet struck Manish in the back, and he was rushed to the hospital. Police have arrested the guard and are investigating the incident further.

title: Now, just one visit for NEET-UG counselling
content: NEET-UG counselling now requires only one physical reporting for candidates seeking admission. Aspirants can complete subsequent document verification online while retaining their allotted seats. The Medical Counselling Committee also introduced online resignation for surrendered seats. NRI category admissions are now fully digitized, improving verification processes. The government aims for a transparent and merit-based counselling system.

title: How Novak Djokovic turned family sacrifice and hardship into tennis greatness
content: Novak Djokovic’s journey to becoming a 24-time Grand Slam champion started long before he won major titles. Growing up during war, living through financial hardship and watching his parents sacrifice everything shaped his mindset. Today, he continues to credit those experiences and his family’s unwavering support for giving him the determination that helped him reach the top of world tennis.

title: Lok Sabha passes anti-paper leak bill after row over Rahul's remarks
content: The Lok Sabha passed a bill to make paper leak punishments more stringent. This legislation aims to expedite trials and deter unfair means in public examinations. The bill proposes significant jail terms and hefty fines for individuals involved in paper leaks. Investigations into paper leak cases are to be completed within two months. The government also highlighted an increase in universities and higher education institutions.

title: Rahul Gandhi remarks row: BJP hits back, calls Congress MP's claim 'a pack of lies'
content: The BJP strongly objects if Rahul Gandhi called students an idiot.  They welcome the remark if it was self-directed by the Congress leader.  BJP leaders accused Rahul Gandhi of spreading falsehoods and misleading the nation.  They stated no bullets were fired during the student protests.  The party highlighted government dialogue and efforts to strengthen laws against paper leaks.

title: No district affected by Naxalism anymore: Ministry of home affairs
content: The number of Left-wing extremism-affected districts has fallen to zero by March 2026. This marks a significant reduction from 126 districts prior to April 2018.  Maoist violence has seen a steep decline, with few incidents recorded this year.  Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand remain the only states with reported Maoist incidents.  However, 37 districts are still classified as legacy and thrust areas.

title: Amid opposition walkout, Rajya Sabha gives approval to Vande Mataram bill
content: The Rajya Sabha passed a bill proposing jail time for disrupting Vande Mataram. Opposition MPs walked out, demanding a statement on police action against protesters. Junior home minister Nityanand Rai piloted the bill, criticizing Congress's stance on the national song. MP Sanjay Singh questioned the RSS's past refusal to hoist the tricolour. AIADMK MPs noted the practice of playing state anthems after national songs.

title: Delhi high court refuses HPV shots stay, but seeks Centre's response
content: The Delhi High Court declined to halt the HPV immunisation campaign. Authorities must now explain the vaccine's introduction within four weeks. The court emphasized the need for proper protocols before administering vaccines. A Public Interest Litigation raised concerns about long-term safety and consent. The next hearing for this matter is scheduled for October 29.

title: Government: North-east cartels shifting towards synthetic drugs
content: Northeast drug syndicates are shifting towards synthetic drugs from Myanmar. They are increasingly using social media and encrypted apps for coordination. Traffickers exploit porous borders and forest routes for cross-border smuggling. Narcotics are concealed in legitimate cargo and passenger vehicles. Moreh-Tamu border remains a key transit point for these drugs.

title: Pathologist's claims raise fresh questions over Nolan Wells' final hours and death
content: Nolan Wells' death has sparked shockwaves across the nation as the cause behind it remains unknown. Amid this, a new claim has been made by a pathologist.

title: Here's why many MBBS graduates can't take foreign licensing exams
content: Thousands of MBBS graduates cannot take foreign licensing exams. Their colleges have not secured ECFMG sponsor notes for global recognition. This formal note is essential for students seeking international medical practice opportunities. Many students discover this issue only after completing their medical degrees. The National Medical Commission is processing updates for several Indian medical colleges.

title: With 90 out of 128 cos & 64% of investments, K'taka top beneficiary of Centre's EDF scheme
content: Karnataka received the most funding from the central government's Electronics Development Fund.  The fund's associated venture funds invested over Rs 1,335 crore in 128 companies.  Karnataka-based firms secured Rs 854.5 crore, representing nearly two-thirds of total investments.  Telangana, Maharashtra, and Delhi also saw significant investments in technology startups.  The fund, managed by Canbank Venture Capital Fund, is now in its divestment phase.

title: No ban on Jagannath movie, artists must enjoy creative liberty, says Supreme Court
content: The Supreme Court rejected a plea to ban an animated film on Mahaprabhu Jagannath.  Justices emphasized artists' creative expression and tolerance for depicting deities.  They noted that preventing such depictions would halt many religious television programs.  The court stated that the Censor Board's approval meant no judicial interference was needed.  It refused to restrict artistic creativity based on the objections of a few.

title: Jeff Bezos' quote on moving heavy, polluting industries to space and the future of travel
content: Sustainable tourism is essential for preserving Earth's natural beauty for future generations.  Healthy ecosystems are vital for the travel experiences that inspire millions of people.  Conscious travelers are increasingly choosing eco-friendly options and reducing waste.  Space technology offers practical ways to enhance travel safety and environmental management.  Protecting our planet ensures that Earth remains a beautiful destination for all.

title: 'Iran is going to get a beating': Trump threatens 'hard' response after attack on US base
content: United States President Donald Trump warned Iran of a forceful military response. American bases in Jordan faced missile attacks which the US intercepted. Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed responsibility for the attempted surprise strike. US and Saudi forces also conducted overnight strikes against Iran-backed militias. Global markets reacted to the latest escalation in the Middle East.

title: Indian Embassy in US slams foreign media for misleading headline over PoK killings
content: The Indian Embassy criticized The New York Times for its inaccurate reporting.  The embassy stated Pakistan illegally occupies parts of Jammu and Kashmir.  Violent clashes have occurred in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir since early June.  Protests are ongoing over regional legislative assembly seats and alleged manipulation.  India attributes these protests to Pakistan's economic exploitation and oppression.

title: D4vd eligible for death penalty as prosecutors review Celeste Rivas murder case
content: Singer D4vd, David Anthony Burke, faces potential death penalty charges. Prosecutors are weighing the death penalty for the murder of Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Burke has pleaded not guilty to all serious charges against him. The case moves forward after a judge found sufficient evidence for trial. His next court hearing is scheduled for August 31 in Los Angeles.

title: IPS Trainee Accused Of Sexually Harassing Colleague In Hyderabad Arrested
content: The accused IPS trainee officer earlier worked as a police constable and later joined IPS in 2025 after clearing the UPSC exam.

title: US-Iran War Live Updates: 'Our Time To Respond,' Says Trump As US Launches 'Powerful' Strikes On Iran
content: Iran-US War News Live Updates: Iran's state television reported a US strike in the Piranshahr border area, after the Fars news agency reported a missile hit an uninhabited area, causing no casualties.

title: Man Loses Rs 8 Lakh To Fake Trading App, Case Against Google India Officer
content: The victim stated that fraudsters contacted him through a social media platform in July and the administrators "advised" him to invest through the trading app after opening an account.

title: Why Russia Is Seeking Telegram Founder Pavel Durov's Arrest
content: Russia announced on Wednesday that it was seeking the arrest of Telegram founder Pavel Durov over accusations of "complicity in terrorism", alleging he had let the platform be used for recruitment by Ukraine's security services.

title: US Puts Indian Man Amritpal Singh On "Most Wanted" List In Drug Case
content: According to the FBI, Amritpal Singh is wanted for his alleged role in the Ravinder Dhanda organised crime group, a transnational criminal network based in Vancouver, Canada.

title: Over 30 Lakh Delhi Homes Getting Piped Water, 6-Month e-KYC Drive Announced
content: The DJB board also approved a series of projects aimed at cleaning the Yamuna, expanding Delhi's sewage-treatment capacity and strengthening the city's water infrastructure.

title: Woman Shot Dead By Unidentified Gunmen In Delhi: Cops
content: A woman was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in the Keshavpuram area of the national capital in the early hours of Thurday.

title: 7 Killed In Helicopter Crash In Argentina: Officials
content: Seven people died when a firefighting helicopter in Argentina's western San Juan province crashed on Wednesday, a local official said.

title: Russia Striking Ukraine's Kyiv With Ballistic Missiles: Mayor
content: Russia was striking the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv with ballistic missiles in the early hours of Thursday, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said in a Telegram post, asking people to seek shelter.

title: Author Salman Rushdie's Attacker Hadi Matar Convicted On Terrorism Charges
content: The man who stabbed and partially blinded author Salman Rushdie on stage at a New York arts institute in 2022 was found guilty on Wednesday of federal terrorism charges stemming from the attack.

title: Magnitude 3.8 Earthquake Hits Maharashtra's Nashik
content: An earthquake of magnitude 3.8 jolted Nashik in Maharashtra in the early hours of Thursday, according to the National Center for Seismology (NCS).

title: Assam Floods: 78 Dead So Far, Over 21,000 Hectares Of Crop Land Damaged
content: The death count in the Assam floods rose to 78, with seven districts currently affected by floods, according to the latest data.

title: Trump Says He Would Be "Quite Disappointed" If China Sells Weapons To Iran
content: US President Donald Trump has stated that he would be "disappointed" if China supplied weapons to Iran, reiterating assurances he said Chinese President Xi Jinping had personally given him that Beijing would not sell arms to Tehran.

title: Zelensky Says Massive Russian Airstrikes Overnight Likely On Ukraine
content: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky warned on Wednesday that Russia would likely carry out another massive attack on the country overnight, in a message posted on social media.

title: 5 Cops Killed, Dozens Injured In Terrorist Attack In Pakistan
content: Militants attacked a police post in northwestern Pakistan on Wednesday, triggering a gunbattle that killed five police officers and wounded about two dozen others, officials said.

title: After Row Over PM Modi's Video, Meta Writes To Centre, Outlines Safeguards
content: Outlining the enhanced safeguards for PM Modi's posts, Meta has said that prominent accounts to get additional oversight. Going forward, only senior Meta officials will vet such posts, sources said.

title: Trump, Netanyahu Explored All Iran Options Including Attack: Israeli Official
content: Netanyahu did not tell Trump that Israel's preference was for an attack on Iran, the official said in a briefing with reporters after the two men met in the White House on Tuesday.

title: 11-Year-Old Rape Survivor Gives Birth To Baby Girl In Haryana
content: A police official mentioned that the girl's family has consented to hand over the newborn to the Child Welfare Committee.

title: No Vada Pav, Samosa In And Near Maharashtra Schools: Food Body's Diktat
content: Foods high in fat, trans-fat, sugar and salt, commonly known as HFSS foods, can no longer be sold, given away or promoted within school premises or within a 50-metre radius of them.

content: Anita Dipke said that the intimidation forced the parents to flee their home and take shelter at a relative's residence in the Konkan region for 16 days

title: Karnataka getting ready for Tamil Nadu CM C. Joseph Vijay’s possible visit
content: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said, “Mr. Vijay has written to the Karnataka Chief Secretary and has also spoken to me over phone. I have extended him the respect he deserves and invited him to the meeting in Bengaluru. It is our duty to receive guests visiting our State with due courtesy, and all necessary arrangements have been made to receive him.”

content: Multiple reports of people, including minors, being detained or arrested by the police, and social media users being asked to take down posts related to the demonstrations have come to the fore

content: Bihar Government targets opening 25 new sugar mills in the next five years in Bihar, says Minister. Bihar Sugar Industry Investment Promotion Policy-2026 to facilitate setting up of an integrated sugar complex.

content: The festival is being organised by the Department of Information and Public Relations (DIPR) of the J&K government in collaboration with National Film Development Corporation (NFDC).

content: While the Bill seeks to curb exam malpractice through time-bound investigations and speedy trials, similar legal timelines have often been missed amid mounting case backlogs

content: Nod for creation of 19 posts of District & Additional Sessions Judge for Exclusive Special Courts; Three posts of DASJ created for Additional Special Courts

title: Parliament Committee calls for upgrading washery infrastructure to spur domestic higher-quality coal production
content: The Standing Committee on Coal, Mines and Steel noted in their latest report that many washeries of Coal India have outlived their designed operational life and are constrained by legacy technology.

content: Association demands that a Syndicate meeting be convened without further delay to approve pending appointments and promotions

content: The suspected narcotic substances were seized over the past one year as part of the ongoing anti-drug crackdown

content: Govts. of Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, U.P., Rajasthan asked to ensure monitoring of paddy cultivation areas, especially identified hotspot villages and fire-prone locations; conduct drone surveys from 3 p.m. to 9 p.m., when attempts to evade satellite detection are more likely, pollution watchdog also says

content: Although the meeting extended for nearly six hours, this has been the least number of resolutions passed in the recent years

title: Textile associations demand measures to reduce power costs in T.N.
content: Southern India Mills Association says the textile industry, which is labour-intensive, will benefit from a hybrid incentive structure that combines upfront capital subsidy, power tariff support, and technology upgrade assistance

content: Madras High Court Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan are slated to hear the case on Thursday

content: International athletes and top Indian paddlers from several States will compete in the four-day event, which will feature over 100 participants

content: CPI(M) leader says reports that appeared in media are part of a “deliberate misinformation campaign” against the party

title: Indian Psychiatric Society urges mental health policy revamp
content: A delegation of psychiatrists met Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan at Thiruvananthapuram and submitted a memorandum seeking reforms in mental healthcare delivery, infrastructure and governance

title: Suspense continues over Karnataka Cabinet expansion as Congress delays final decision
content: Suspense over the expansion of the Karnataka Cabinet continued on Wednesday, with the Congress high command once again deferring a final decision on the list of legislators to be inducted

content: Three persons were arrested shortly after former AIADMK MLA approached the High Court seeking a CBI probe

content: Total business reached ₹35,190 crore as on June 30, 2026, from ₹29,051 crore as on June 30, 2025, recording 21.13 % growth.

content: The new stretch has been laid 3-4 km away from Singarapettai High Road to prevent heavy vehicles from entering Tirupattur town to reach other districts

content: Initial inquiry revealed that special teams were formed in Ranipet to prevent illegal sand mining, smuggling of ganja and other banned substances

content: ACS (Home) ordered restructuring of KPA including all ranks from CPOs to grade SIs, and revamp of KPSOA by including ranks from SI to SP (non-IPS). title: NHAI removes 361 encroachments from national highways after Supreme Court order
content: The nationwide drive ensured a ‘smooth and effective enforcement’ of removing illegal access points, encroachments, unauthorised structures and median cuts along highways, the NHAI said in a statement

title: Karnataka High Court questions conduct of Malur judicial officer on public road; stays FIR registered against three for overtaking her car
content: Taking serious exception to the conduct of a judicial officer on a public road, the High Court of Karnataka stayed the investigation against three persons based on a First Information Report registered against them for allegedly overtaking a private car of the judicial officer at Malur in Kolar district

title: Anti-corruption drive ‘Project Zero’ launched in Kerala
content: Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said that the project is aimed at catching not just bribe takers, but those giving bribes too

content: Being established by Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited, the projects are coming up at Kanekal in Anantapur district and Pattikonda in Kurnool district
